409.q: No, I wasn't nervous about it. John Hammond was helping me in a little way. Not -- in the way that he had. Financially, too. I went to -- down in Texas to get a tenor player.

382.t: Savoy Sultans, Lionel Hampton and a 1948 Pittsburgh show
382.s: Memories of the Savoy Sultans, Rudy Powell and Ralph Cooper's broadcasts.
382.q: Right. In 1948, I believe it was they had 'A Night of Stars' in Pittsburgh and they had Lois Deppe with whom Earl Hines used to play and then they had Billy Eckstine and Errol Garner. They had four generations going for them. Earl had just become popular. Errol Garner. (Deletion)

70.t: Illinois Jacquet and Lionel Hampton's first band
70.s: After a break, Jackson first heard Jacquet in Hampton's 1941 band and lists its saxophones, trumpets, and rhythm section.
70.ch: Musicians of the era: players, drummers, bassists, pianists
70.q: And it was -- the two tenor players was like Mutt and Jeff, here was Dexter Gordon, and Dexter Gordon was so tall and Illinois was short, and they was the two tenor players in there.

454.t: Lionel Hampton years, Mingus Fingers and the bebop song
454.s: Hampton and Red Norvo were the longest jobs; tunes written for Hampton, lost in a bus wreck, and a bebop lyric Hampton disliked.
454.ch: Pedal points, Hampton, Norvo and Debut
454.q: Quite a few tunes with him. He said all that stuff was lost in the bus wreck. What was -- the names [BEBOPS -- see insert] I don't know. Some ballads. One was called (singing). I had this whole thing I wrote out. (Unintelligible) a little thing about bebop. And Lionel didn't want bebop. He said,…

19.t: Illinois Jacquet's rhythm section and joining his octet at the Apollo
19.s: He had furnished Jacquet a rhythm section earlier, and in January 1948 replaces Sir Charles Thompson in the Jacquet group.
19.ch: Trio, Eckstine accompanist and Illinois Jacquet, 1945-48
19.q: So anyway, I left and I came back to Washington. I had been here about I guess three weeks, maybe a month... No, it wasn't, it was about three weeks. And I got this call from Illinois Jacquet. I had met him earlier, right after I had left the Eckstine band, because around that same time he had just…

103.s: Hinton adds Lionel Hampton; Jones says he got Hampton xylophones for speed and advised him to follow Red Norvo.
103.q: Let's leave him with his telephones. Lionel Hampton sit down there with them telephones, those vibraphones. That's it. Telephones. H: Is that what you call them? Jones': Telephones.

239.t: Lionel Hampton's early band at the Grand Terrace and Marshall Royal
239.s: Jones recalls the early Hampton band with Sir Charles Thompson, Marshall Royal and Ray Perry, and Marshall's role helping Basie.
239.ch: Follow-up questions, Bird and the Ellington sidemen
239.q: You know, we fell in love with the Ellington outfit. In fact I think everybody was crazy about Duke, and then -- of course Basie and Lionel Hampton, I think, was one of the guys that really drew some attention at the Grand Terrace. He had quite an outfit. Sir Charles Thompson on piano, Marshall…

13.t: Lionel Hampton as a boy and on the Goodman date
13.s: Hamp humming; got him the session.
13.q: Yeah, we used to go down on the curb, stand around the picket fences and sidewalk. Still humming like he does now. He was humming then.
